physical_harm: Extensive burn injuries resulting in death
number_of_offences: Charged with 2 offences, both upheld by High Court but overturned by Supreme Court
motive: Depression due to inability to join husband at his posting and shame from a photograph with a male stranger
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the deceased died otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and that she had suffered extensive ante-mortem burn injuries, but found that the essential ingredients of dowry death, particularly the demand for dowry and harassment, were not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of PW-1 and PW-2 with skepticism, noting that they treated their daughter's threats as a joke and that their statements changed from the FIR, raising doubts about the truthfulness of the allegations.
bail_history: Appellants are on bail. Their bail bond(s) stand discharged.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 17.01.2007; Trial judgment: 26.04.2012; High Court decision: 26.04.2012; Supreme Court decision: 20 September 2024
legal_representation: A.P. Mohanty, Adv. for the Appellants; Akshat Kumar, Ajay Bahuguna, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Sections 304-B and 498-A IPC; High Court: Affirmed conviction, reduced sentence under Section 304-B IPC to 7 years R.I. and maintained 1 year R.I. under Section 498-A IPC; Supreme Court: Set aside conviction and sentence under Sections 304-B and 498-A IPC
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased's death was a result of cruelty or harassment by the appellants in connection with a dowry demand, and that the presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act should be raised against the accused for dowry death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that there was no direct evidence of dowry demand or harassment by the appellants, and that the deceased's death was likely suicidal due to depression and other personal reasons, not due to any cruelty or harassment by the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the presumption under Section 113-B of the Evidence Act is only raised when all the essential ingredients of dowry death are proved beyond reasonable doubt by the prosecution.
